title.narrative: Uzbekistan: Supporting a Transparent and Inclusive Market Transition

description.narrative: (i) Improving the efficiency, sustainability, and transparency of resource allocation in the economy; and (ii) Enhancing economic inclusion and social resilience.

The development objectives of the Supporting a Transparent and Inclusive Market Transition Development Policy Operation in Uzbekistan are to: (i) improve the efficiency, sustainability, and transparency of resource allocation in the economy; and (ii) enhance economic inclusion and social resilience. The strategy has five pillars: (i) enhancing state and public institutions; (ii) securing the rule of law and reforming the judicial system; (iii) promoting economic development; (iv) fostering social development; and (v) ensuring personal and public security through inter-ethnic and religious tolerance and constructive foreign policy. In early 2019, the Government (with support through the second DPO engagement) adopted a further 2019 - 2021 “Reform Roadmap” to provide further clarity about its reform priorities. It contains five focus areas: (i) maintaining macroeconomic stability; (ii) accelerating the market transition; (iii) strengthening social protection and citizen services; (iv) transforming the Government's role in the market economy; and (v) preserving environmental sustainability.

title.narrative: RI9:The establishment of referral pathways for survivors of gender-based violence.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target for the RI was achieved. </strong>Referral mechanisms have been incorporated within the Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs) for each area (law enforcement, healthcare, psychological and social) and are undergoing the introduction stage nationwide. ???????</p>

title.narrative: RI3: An increase in cotton growing area with adopted climate-smart farm technologies.

comment.narrative: <p>The RI3 was comfortably achieved, as the cotton growing area under climate-smart farm technologies reached 1,258,000 hectares in 2020; 1,819,000 hectares in 2021 (against a target of 300,000 hectares); and 2,293,000 hectares in 2022.</p>

title.narrative: RI8: A decrease in the annual number of people fined by the Government for violations of place of registration rules.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target for the RI was comfortably achieved. </strong>Since 2020 the number of fines have declined dramatically compared to the 2019 baseline of 317,088. Their number increased somewhat in 2022, but it remained comfortably below the target (125,000), which seems not to have been ambitious enough.</p>

title.narrative: RI1: The stock of outstanding loans classified as commercial by the Central Bank of Uzbekistan, as a share of the stock of all outstanding banking sector loans.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target for RI1 was achieved.</strong> By end of 2020, commercial lending by the banking sector, based on the CentralBank’s classification, had increased to 54 percent of total outstanding loans, and by end-2021 it had reached 61 percent, slightly above the target set for the RI (Table 3). Progress was sustained in 2022, with the percentage of commercial lending further increasing to 65 percent by November 2022. The removal from bank balance sheets of UFRD on lending to SOEs contributed significantly to the achievement of the RI target. More than 50 percent of bank loans to SOEs used to be financed, on preferential terms, through on-lending by UFRD. The remaining lending portfolio on non-commercial terms, representing 35 percent of total loans, consists essentially of mortgage loans for social programs. These will be reduced as they mature, as subsidized lending by commercial banks has been discontinued. Eligible borrowers could possibly obtain subsidies through social on-budget programs.</p>

title.narrative: RI7: Increased transparency and accountability of the general government budget.

comment.narrative: <p>The RI of including UFRD income and expenditures into the State Budget reflected the implementation of the prior action and, as such, the target was achieved. ???????</p>

title.narrative: RI2: Number of state-owned commercial banks boards where the majority comprises independent directors, consistent with requirements in the Banking Law.

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>The target for RI2 was achieved</strong>. By the end-2021 the boards of 8 out of 12 state-owned banks comprised a majority of independent directors, against a target of 5. By the end-2022, 7 SOCBs had a majority of independent directors on their boards[1]. Independent directors are selected by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), through interviews, based on their professional qualifications and terms of reference for their positions. Independent directors have had an impact on risk management practices and strategic planning by SOCBs, although it is too early to see a notable change in the performance of SOCBs with a majority of independent directors on their boards.</p>
<p>[1] The slight decrease reflects the replacement of the Board in one bank (Asakabank).</p>

title.narrative: RI4: Retail prices of all unleaded petroleum (AI80 and above) and diesel (including ECO Diesel) are determined by the market and free of direct government subsidies.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The RI reflected the implementation of the prior action and, as such, the target was achieved.</strong> ???????</p>

title.narrative: RI10: A decreasing share of low-income allowance applications with income below the eligibility threshold that are rejected because of lack of registration with the Employment Service Center.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The target for the RI was met.</strong> In 2021 and 2022 the coverage of the low-income allowances has increased substantially, from under 500 thousand to 2.2 million families. Due to this rapid and significant expansion of coverage, the RI has been unstable in 2021, but there is a steadily declining trend into 2022, suggesting that the eligibility conditions are becoming clearer to applicants. At the end of 2021 rejected applications nationwide had reached 37.3 percent, slightly above the target. However, in the last quarter of 2022, rejected applications were consistently below the target, which was therefore met.</p>

title.narrative: RI5: Megawatts of renewable energy generation capacity that have been transparently and competitively tendered as PPPs, consistent with the PPP Law, and whose tender process has been concluded.

comment.narrative: <p>While in 2020 all PPP projects were awarded through direct contracting, in 2021 competitive tenders became prominent, with 5 projects awarded, for a total capacity of 2,597 MW. The target for the RI, set at 300 MW, was thus comfortably met.</p>
